function: Gen-DRL (GAN actor, FC critic) jointly learns HAP trajectory, user-HAP association, beamforming and channel prediction to maximize secrecy energy efficiency in a LEO-HAP downlink (pp. 6-8).
system: LEO satellite UPA (Table 2 lists 265 antennas), three 64-antenna HAP UPAs, 21 users and 21 eavesdroppers with 16-antenna ULAs, 28 GHz, no RIS (pp. 4, 11).
method: Actor-critic deep reinforcement learning: GAN generator with Bi-LSTM as actor, fully connected critic, prioritized experience replay, Adam; 2000 training epochs per setup (pp. 7-9, 11).
data_channel: Custom simulated LEO and HAP channels (Nakagami-m stated, Rician factor 10 dB, 5 paths, Doppler, delay, atmospheric loss); users and eavesdroppers uniformly placed; no 3GPP model (pp. 4-5, 11).
test_conditions: Each experimental setup trained for 2000 epochs; sweeps of HAP power, rate threshold, number of HAPs, users per HAP, altitude; no train-then-test in unseen conditions (pp. 11-13).
baselines: Learned: LSTM-DDQN [31] and DDQN [38]; non-learned: exhaustive-search optimal solution as upper bound; no other classical heuristic (pp. 10, 12-13).
metrics: Secrecy energy efficiency versus HAP power, rate threshold, number of HAPs, users per HAP and altitude; reward convergence; gap to optimal, 5.1% for Gen-DRL (pp. 11-13).
complexity: Complexity per iteration O(KH + M^3 + HT + bm|theta|), total over I iterations and L agents; contrasted with LSTM-DDQN, DDQN, genetic search, exhaustive search; no runtime (pp. 9-10).
openness: none: no code or data link; simulations in Python 3.8.5 and PyTorch 2.0 on the authors' own machine (pp. 10-11).
q1_support: p. 4: "adopt Nakagami-m fading for a more accurate representation"; the channel is a custom model with Rician factor, Doppler, delay and atmospheric loss (Table 2, page 11). No 3GPP TR 38.811 or 38.901, DeepMIMO or measured data is mentioned.
q2_support: p. 11: "was subjected to an extensive training duration of 2000" epochs for each experimental setup. The sweeps over HAP power, rate threshold, number of HAPs, users per HAP and altitude never say a model trained in one setting was tested in another.
q3_support: p. 10: "Optimal solution: in which we design an exhaustive" search (non-learned), plus the learned LSTM-DDQN [31] and DDQN [38]; all are compared on secrecy energy efficiency in Figs. 5-9 (pages 12-13).
q4_support: p. 9: "computational complexity per iteration can be expressed as:" followed on page 10 by O(KH + M^3 + HT + bm|theta|) per iteration and the total over I iterations and L agents (Eqs. 25-26).
q5_support: p. 10: "The simulations were implemented using Python 3.8.5 and" PyTorch 2.0 on the authors' own machine; the paper gives no link to code or data and uses no public dataset.
notes: Included, area 6: Gen-DRL outputs beamforming (physical layer) jointly with HAP trajectory and user association (above the physical layer) and channel prediction. Under the satellite and aerial rule this passes above_phy, and NTN is more specific than areas 2 and 3. The system has no RIS (Fig. 1, page 4); Algorithm 2 on page 9 lists RIS among its inputs and some references are RIS-aided, but the model has none. The non-learned baseline is the exhaustive-search optimum. Complexity is asymptotic only, with no runtime.
